title: Sparse coloring for isosceles-free grids: an AI-assisted proof case study
summary: We study the largest size $C(n)$ of a subset of the $n\times n$ integer grid containing no isosceles triple, including equally spaced collinear triples. We prove $C(n)=Ω\left(n\sqrt{\log\log n/\log n}\right)$ by applying the sparse hypergraph coloring theorem of Cooper and Mubayi. Elementary geometry and primitive-direction counts give maximum degree $O(n^2\log n)$ and pair-codegree at most $5n$ for the forbidden-triple hypergraph.
